correctness.rationale: The descendant collision condition is equivalent to a C4. The pair-count inequality gives the sharp 16-edge ceiling. Equality leaves only three candidate degree sequences; two are eliminated by parity/intersection arguments, while the surviving (3,3,3,3,2,2) case forces one uncovered pair and the three perfect matchings of K4. This proves uniqueness and Fano completion. The labeled count 15*3*2*6!=64,800 and orbit-stabilizer calculation are exact. The embedded verifier independently finds zero 17-edge cases, 90 normalized 16-edge row multisets, 64,800 labeled maxima, one natural orbit, and stabilizer 16.

value.rationale: The q=6 length-two case is a natural exact benchmark in the foundational separable-code/Zarankiewicz correspondence, and the literature already singles out exact short-length codes as building blocks for longer constructions. Classifying every equality case is structurally meaningful: it shows the numerical optimum is rigid, identifies the unique Fano-deletion geometry, and gives the complete labeled and symmetry census. This is not a parameter renaming or recomputation of the known value 16.
